messages:
maya: Heads up — Acme wants a temporary safelist to forward traffic to their Dedicated pool for an upcoming load test. They want a simple toggle in console + API. Any strong opinions on how the adhoc safelist/forwarding UX should work?

raj: +1 for a short-lived 'forwarding' override. Current org allowlist flow is too heavy for this. Key requirements: TTL, owner, audit event, and a clear signal in metrics.

lucy: API-first please. We should reuse header semantics (org header + override token) rather than inventing a new route type. Also must ensure RBAC checks so only support/solutions can flip it.

samir: operational risk: if we route big traffic to Dedicated it may exhaust their reserved pools or blow committed throughput. We need cost/usage guardrails and an automatic fallback if capacity is low. Also emit a tagso that billing jobs catch it.

deploy-bot: FYI created draft spec: <https://redwood.internal/specs/overrides|spec: adhoc-forwarding> (WIP) :eyes:

alex: UX notes — toggles are misunderstood. Suggest a modal: "Adhoc Forwarding" with fields: target (dedicated/hosted), TTL (ISO), owner (email), reason, preview routes impacted, and a list of dependent policies (quotas, rate limits). Show estimated cost delta before confirm.

raj: Example header we could accept for API clients:
```
X-Redwood-Org-Override: forward_to=dedicated;token=xxxx;expires=2024-08-05T15:00:00Z
```
This should be auditable and we should normalize it into a structured DB event.

maya: On the console side I want a one-click Preview that runs the route matcher against a sample of recent traffic and shows percent of requests that would have flipped. Also an opt-in telemetry checkbox (for safety).

lucy: Policy question — do we allow per-route overrides as well or only org-level? Per-route is more flexible but increases complexity for policy evaluation. My vote: start org-level only, add route-granularity later.

samir: Telemetry labels to add: routing.override=true, routing.override.owner=<email>, routing.override.ttl=<ts>, routing.target=dedicated/hosted, cost. Also emit an alert if routed volume > X% of total for > Y minutes.

maya: I'll prototype a small admin endpoint to create overrides:
```json
POST /v1/admin/routing/overrides
{
  "org_id": "acme-corp",
  "target": "dedicated-pool-42",
  "ttl": "2024-08-05T15:00:00Z",
  "owner": "maya@redwood.ai",
  "reason": "acme load test - short-lived"
}
```
Make sure it returns an audit id and preview snapshot.

deploy-bot: Draft PR posted: <https://git.redwood/infra/pull/1234|infra#1234> — includes DB schema + event hooks.

alex: s/concerns — we also need a revoke action and a TTL expiry job that emits an event when an override expires. Consider soft-delete for forensic audit.

lucy: Agree. Also require a signed justification in enterprise plan (checkbox + free-text) for compliance.

maya: Great. I'll wire up a proto in the console and bounce the spec off policy & billing. Sync at 15:00 PT? :clock3: everyone available?

raj: I can make it. samir can you join for capacity/billing guardrails?

samir: yes, will join.

deploy-bot: Meeting invite sent -> #eng-platform. PR and spec links in thread.
